name: St. Stephen's College
awards: NAAC: A+ (Cycle 3); UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
studentUnionStatus: Active - St. Stephen's College Union; elections held annually; constitution available on college website
shortHistory: Founded in 1881 by the Anglican Church Missionary Society, St. Stephen's College is one of the oldest and most prestigious colleges in Delhi. Established during the British colonial era, it was named after Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr. The college was originally located near Kashmere Gate before moving to its current campus in North Campus. It has consistently been ranked among the top colleges in India for arts and sciences. The college maintains its Christian character while welcoming students of all faiths. Its alumni include numerous prominent figures in politics, civil services, academia, and the arts. The college union is active and follows a democratic election process. The campus features heritage architecture and a vibrant intellectual culture.

name: Hindu College
awards: NAAC: A+ (Cycle 3); UGC "Heritage College"; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
studentUnionStatus: Active - Registered student council; current president & secretary listed on college "Student Body" page. Elections biannual (morning/evening). Constitution available via DU portal.
shortHistory: Established in 1899 by nationalist leaders Lala Sundar Das and Motilal Nehru as Delhi College, it merged with Delhi University in 1922. Founded by the Sanatan Dharma Sabha during the British colonial era, the college emerged as a hub for progressive thought and nationalist consciousness. It is renowned as an all-rounder institution excelling in science, arts, and commerce. The college was awarded UGC's "College with Potential for Excellence" and recognized as a "Heritage College" for its historical significance. Alumni include prominent figures in politics, civil services, and academia. The campus continues to be a vibrant center of intellectual discourse and cultural activity in North Campus.

name: Lady Irwin College
awards: NAAC: A (Cycle 3); UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
studentUnionStatus: Active - Lady Irwin College Students' Union; elections held annually
shortHistory: Founded in 1932 by the All India Women's Conference (AIWC), Lady Irwin College was established to provide higher education in home science and related disciplines for women. Named after Lady Irwin, the wife of the then Viceroy of India, the college was initially located in the Viceregal Estate. It was the first institution in India to offer degree courses in home science. The college moved to its current campus near Sikandra Road in 1938. It has played a pioneering role in women's education and research in nutrition, textile science, and child development. The college maintains an active student union and continues to be a leading institution for home science education in India.

name: Miranda House
awards: NAAC: A++ (Cycle 3); Top women's college ranking
studentUnionStatus: Active - Established Student Council. Office-bearers named on "Student Societies" page. Elections yearly (DU academic calendar). Constitutions linked in DU archives.
shortHistory: Founded on 8 February 1948 as Delhi University's first women's college, Miranda House was established by the government to expand women's education in post-independence India. Named after educator Sarojini Naidu (Miranda), its first Principal was Dr. Leela Mukherjee. The college quickly became top-ranked for science and humanities programs. Miranda House has consistently maintained its position at the forefront of women's education, producing generations of women leaders across diverse fields.

name: Kirori Mal College (KMC)
awards: NAAC: A (Cycle 3); UGC-PUCE award (2016); DBT-Star College Scheme
studentUnionStatus: Active - KMC Students' Council (morning & evening) is active. President and secretaries listed in annual handbook. Elections each year (online nomination). Constitution available via DU portal.
shortHistory: Established in 1954 by Sindhi philanthropists through the Sri Kirori Mal College Trust, the college was founded to serve the educational needs of post-Partition refugee communities in Delhi. Named after philanthropist Sri Kirori Mal, it quickly gained renown for strong arts and science programs, particularly its drama and dance societies. The college was awarded the DBT-Star College Scheme and UGC's "College with Potential for Excellence" (PUCE) in 2016. Alumni include politicians like Ajay Maken.

name: Ramjas College
awards: NAAC: A+ (Cycle 3); National Award to Principal (2019)
studentUnionStatus: Active - Union exists (Ramjas Student Council). Current list of president, sec., joint sec. published on student page. Elections yearly. Student constitution PDF on college site.
shortHistory: Founded in 1917 in memory of philanthropist Lala Ramjas, the college was established by the DAV College Trust rooted in the Arya Samaj movement. It merged with Delhi University in 1922 and shared early faculty with Delhi College of Engineering. Ramjas College holds the distinction of being the site of India's first student strike in 1920, marking the beginning of student political activism in the country. The current campus was established in 1950. Noted for its activism and strong academic programs, the college received the National Award to Principal in 2019.

shortHistory: Founded in 1948 by the DAV College Managing Committee, Hansraj College was established in the post-independence period to meet the growing demand for higher education in Delhi. Named after Mahatma Hansraj, a pioneer of the DAV movement and the first principal of the first DAV school. The college has grown to become one of the largest constituent colleges of Delhi University, known for its strong programs in science, commerce, and arts. It has produced numerous alumni who have excelled in various fields including politics, cinema, and business.
